The round-2 fix (spawn_monitor + 10s hard bound around the whole distributed-node bootstrap) did NOT resolve the Windows hang either -- a 3rd CI round on commit 6aa7ccd96, then a 4th bare re-run of the identical commit, both hung the full 600s with zero output. Escalated to Fable for adjudication after 4 CI rounds without a Windows environment to reproduce locally. Fable's source-verified diagnosis (against OTP's win32 sys.c, epmd.c, erlexec.c): the hang is OUTSIDE any test body -- eunit's own per-test {timeout,30,...} already bounds net_kernel:start/peer/erpc (round 1's 70s partial-progress failure proves this). The actual mechanism is open_port({spawn_executable, epmd}, ...) tying epmd.exe to this BEAM's port table; exit(Pid,kill) on the bounding worker (or eunit's own cancel) can hit the win32 spawn driver's uninterruptible TerminateProcess+WaitForSingleObject(INFINITE) teardown path. Also identified scripts/test_gateway.py's subprocess.run(stdout=PIPE) as non-streaming despite its docstring's claim otherwise -- the 'zero output' in every failed run was uninformative, not evidence of an early hang, invalidating the reasoning behind both prior fix attempts.
